Cost Share: Pre-Award

From the ORA eTraining module "It Takes a Village: Understanding Cost Share on Sponsored Projects" (lesson 4 of 7).
Pre Award Planning
Cost sharing at Morgan State University is a significant, long-term commitment that spans the entire lifecycle of a project, from inception through closeout. Meeting these obligations is essential to maintain federal compliance and uphold our institutional commitment to supporting research. Carefully review the following steps to ensure that all necessary actions are taken prior to submitting any proposal with cost-sharing requirements.
Cost Share: Pre-Award Phase
All proposals for sponsored projects must be routed through ORA prior to submission. The Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR) is the only individual authorized to submit applications and accept awards on behalf of MSU.
Step #1: Submit an Internal Routing Form (IRF)
For any proposal submission, a prospective PI must complete an Internal Routing Form (IRF) to provide necessary preliminary information to ORA & the Office of Restricted Funds Accounting (RFA). When a project has mandatory or voluntary committed cost share the PI must check the corresponding box on the IRF.
Step #2: Review Budget with ORA Budget Specialist
During the proposal preparation phase, the ORA Budget Specialist will review the FOA and IRF. If cost share commitments are present, they will ask the PI for elements of cost share and will work with the PI to prepare a budget and budget justification. These documents will be included in the proposal submission.
Step #3: Chair & Dean Approval
If an award has mandatory or voluntary committed cost share, the budget and budget justification must be approved by the PI’s Chair and Dean and provided to the ORA no later than one week prior to the project’s submission deadline.
Step #4: 3rd Party Cost Share
For third party cost share, the PI will be required to provide ORA & RFA with documentation detailing the commitment from the external entity. The PI should provide this documentation no later than one week prior to the proposal submission deadline. Valuation of 3rd party cost share should be in line with market value for similar goods & services.
